transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I guess what brings me in is that I keep getting these thoughts at work—like if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, then someone could get hurt or lose everything. I know that probably sounds extreme, and part of me does know it’s not completely rational, but in the moment it feels like it’s on me personally, like I’m responsible, and I can’t really just move on from it. Does that make sense?
When you have these thoughts, how do they affect your ability to function at work or in other areas of your life?

It’s… affecting things more than I’d like to admit, honestly. I mean, I’m still showing up and trying to be useful, but there was a major cloud migration deadline that I missed because I just couldn’t get myself to sign off on some decisions. I kept needing to recheck or make sure I wasn’t missing something.

And I think my team has noticed. They’ve started kind of working around me instead of relying on me, which is… hard to say out loud. I don’t think they’re being cruel or anything, but it’s not how it used to be.

Outside of work, I’ve been telling myself I’m just busy, but I’ve stopped going to basketball and salsa nights. Those were kind of the things that kept me connected and grounded, and I’ve let them slip. I know that probably sounds bad. I’m trying not to make excuses.
Outside of these specific work-related thoughts you've been having, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there's no immediate problem or deadline?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to separate it, honestly. I wouldn’t say I’m just worried about everything all the time, if that’s what you mean. It feels more tied to those situations where I think I might miss something important.

I mean, I probably do run a little tense in general, but I’ve always kind of thought of that as being conscientious, you know? I don’t want to overstate it. Most of the time it’s not like there’s some random worry out of nowhere—it’s more when something could go wrong and I feel like I should have caught it. Does that answer the question?
Do you ever find yourself having thoughts that feel intrusive or unwanted, that cause you significant distress or anxiety, even if you try to ignore or suppress them?

Yeah… I think that is probably the best way to describe it. They’re not thoughts I want to have, and I do try to push them aside, but they kind of come back hard.

It’s usually like, “What if I missed one setting?” or “What if there’s one access rule I didn’t catch?” or some warning sign I should’ve noticed. And then my mind jumps to, you know, someone could get hurt or lose everything because I didn’t do my job right. I know that sounds dramatic, and part of me does know it’s not fully rational, but in the moment it really feels like it’s on me personally.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that right, but I can’t just ignore it and move on the way I probably should.

When you have these intrusive thoughts, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, mentally reviewing events, or trying to ‘neutralize’ the thought in some way?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just being thorough, but it goes past that sometimes.

I’ll reread deployment plans and audit logs over and over, and then if I’m still not feeling okay about it, I’ll go back through old messages too, like maybe there was something I missed. Even with things like door locks, I’ll check more than once.

And there’s this mental thing I do where I count through the steps in my head until they feel… I don’t know, safe, I guess. That sounds strange when I say it out loud.

I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves because stopping before it feels complete makes me panic. I know that’s not ideal. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything—I just feel like if I stop too soon, something bad could happen.
When you check things repeatedly or count through steps in your head, is it more to reduce the anxiety that comes with the thought, or to prevent something bad from actually happening?

I think… both, honestly. I’d like to say it’s just to calm myself down, and that’s definitely part of it, because the anxiety gets really uncomfortable if I stop too soon.

But in the moment it also feels like I’m actually preventing something bad from happening. Like if I reread the deployment plan one more time, or go back through the audit logs or old messages, then I’ll catch the thing that would’ve caused a problem. Same with locks sometimes—I know it probably looks excessive, but it feels irresponsible not to check.

And the counting through steps in my head is kind of the same. I’m looking for that feeling of, okay, it’s safe now. If I don’t get that feeling, I panic a bit, and I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone left because stopping before it felt complete just felt… wrong. I know that may not be the best answer, but that’s how it feels.

Do these intrusive thoughts and the things you do to manage them—like checking or counting—happen even when there’s no actual work or responsibility that requires it, or do they usually come up in response to real-life stressors or tasks?

It usually starts with something real, I think — like a task, a setting, an access rule, some warning sign I’m supposed to notice. I don’t want to make it sound like it comes out of nowhere all the time.

But then it… grows beyond what’s actually required, if that makes sense. What brings me in is that I’ll get stuck on, “What if I missed just one thing?” and then my mind jumps straight to someone getting hurt or losing everything because of me. Even when part of me knows that’s probably not rational, it feels like I’m personally responsible and I can’t just move on.

I hope that answers what you’re asking. It’s not that there’s always a real emergency — it’s more that my brain treats it like there is.
Do these intrusive thoughts and the behaviors you use to manage them, like checking or counting, ever happen even when there isn’t a real task or responsibility that triggers them?

Yeah… I think it can happen even when there isn’t something that truly requires it. I don’t want to overstate it, because a lot of the time there is some real task or responsibility in the background.

But what brings me in is that I keep getting stuck on this thought that if I miss one setting, one access rule, one warning sign, then someone could get hurt or lose everything. And even though part of me knows that’s probably not rational, it feels like it’s on me personally, like I can’t just move on until I’m sure.

I’m not sure if I’m explaining that the right way, but that’s the part that feels… out of proportion.
Have you ever had these kinds of anxious or intrusive thoughts in situations where there’s no work or responsibility involved—like when you’re relaxing, daydreaming, or doing something you enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like it’s constant or like I’m just sitting there imagining disasters all day, but it can show up even when I’m not actively working.

It’s usually the same kind of thought, though — like, what if I missed one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, and because of that someone gets hurt or loses everything. And I know, at least part of me knows, that it’s probably not rational in that moment. But it hits me like it’s personally on me, like I can’t really relax or move on until I’ve somehow made sure.

I’m not sure if that’s what you mean, but yes, it can intrude even when I’m trying to do something normal or enjoyable.
Outside of work, do these intrusive thoughts cause you significant distress or interfere with your ability to enjoy activities, spend time with loved ones, or function in other areas of your life?

Yeah… I guess it does, more than I’d like to admit.

I’ve been trying to tell myself it’s just me being thorough, but I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I couldn’t finish signing off on decisions. I kept getting stuck, and eventually my team started sort of working around me instead of relying on me. That’s… hard to say out loud.

And outside work, I’ve stopped showing up for basketball and salsa nights. Those were things that helped me feel normal and connected, and I keep telling myself I’m just busy or tired, but I’m losing those routines and the people around them.

So yes, it is interfering. I’m sorry, I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but it’s not just in my head at work anymore.

Have you ever had intrusive thoughts or felt driven to do things over and over, even in areas of life completely unrelated to work or responsibilities—like at home, while driving, or during conversations?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s fair to say. I wish I could say it’s only at work, but it kind of spills over.

I’ll reread things over and over — deployment plans, audit logs, but also old messages, even when there’s no real reason to. At home I can get stuck checking door locks more than I need to. And sometimes I’m not even physically checking something, I’m just counting through steps in my head until it feels… safe, I guess.

I know that probably sounds excessive. I don’t mean that I want to be doing it. It’s more like if I stop before it feels complete, I get this panic feeling, like I’m leaving something dangerous unfinished. I’ve even stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves because I couldn’t make myself stop yet.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you ever had intrusive thoughts or felt the need to do certain things repeatedly—like checking, counting, or trying to feel safe—when there is no work or responsibility involved at all, such as during downtime at home or while interacting with family or friends?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s not only when there’s an actual task in front of me.

I’ll reread things I’ve already checked, like deployment plans or audit logs, but also door locks at home, or even old messages, when there isn’t really a reason to. Sometimes I’m just going through steps in my head, counting them out until they feel… safe, I guess.

It’s embarrassing to say, because I know it sounds like too much. But if I stop before it feels complete, I get this panicky feeling, like I’m leaving something unfinished that could turn bad. There have been times I stayed at the office for hours after everyone else left because I couldn’t quite make myself stop.

Is that… is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you ever find yourself doing things like checking, counting, or repeating actions even when you aren’t having one of those intrusive thoughts or worrying about something specific?

Yeah… sometimes, I think. Not always because there’s a specific thought attached to it.

It’s more like I’ll start rereading a deployment plan or an audit log, or checking a door lock, or even looking back at old messages, and I can’t quite stop until it feels right or safe. Sometimes I’m counting through the steps in my head, even if I couldn’t point to one clear worry in that moment.

I know that probably sounds a bit… excessive. But if I stop before it feels complete, I get panicky. I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else left because I couldn’t make myself end the checking yet.

Is that what you mean?
